name: Shulman UTM Attribution for Elementor
author: Ranel Shulman

sections.description:
Production-grade attribution and analytics plugin for Elementor Forms and WooCommerce with advanced customer journey tracking and reporting.

Tracks first-touch and last-touch attribution across the customer journey, captures Elementor leads, enriches WooCommerce orders, records WooCommerce shopping events, and provides analytics dashboards with CSV export.

Features:
* Elementor lead attribution with complete conversion snapshots
* WooCommerce order attribution
* WooCommerce Analytics Dashboard
* Executive Dashboard with KPIs
* Orders Analytics
* Cart Events tracking
* Product Performance reports
* Funnel Analytics
* Campaign Performance reports
* First-touch and Last-touch attribution
* Session tracking with visit count
* Attribution confidence classification
* UTM cookie persistence and server-side fallback
* Advanced Leads Dashboard with filters, sorting, custom columns and CSV export
* Manually correct a lead’s contact details and UTM values, individually or in bulk across multiple leads at once
* Historical Attribution Repair — rebuild “untracked” records whose original landing page already contains attribution parameters
* Landing Page Optimization Report with canonical Source/Medium grouping, full column sorting, period-over-period comparisons, Top Insights, Top Rankings, Paid vs Organic breakdown, and a simple Report Notes field
* Read-only Reporting REST API for connecting external reporting, analytics, and business intelligence platforms
* Separate WooCommerce analytics database optimized for reporting
* Plugin-wide canonical Meta (Facebook/Instagram) normalization shown consistently across every report, dashboard, and export, with a Debug Layer to inspect the original captured value when needed
* Fully backward compatible with legacy cookies, options and meta keys
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin ZIP in WordPress admin or copy the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Configure settings from the plugin admin screen.
sections.changelog:
Note: this section is kept trimmed to recent versions to stay under WordPress.org’s 5000-character
changelog limit. The complete version history is preserved in docs/CHANGELOG-ARCHIVE.md.

1.27.3

  • Fixed: a Google Ads landing URL that someone copied and shared on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp or another social/messaging app was credited to “google / paid” for every visitor who clicked it (all carrying the original ad click’s gclid). A gclid arriving from a social or messaging referrer is now credited to that referring channel (e.g. “facebook / social”), and the copied campaign values are dropped. Also detected inside the Facebook/Instagram in-app browser when no referrer is sent. Affects new visits only.
  • Fixed: returning from a payment gateway or 3-D Secure page (Grow, Cardcom, PayPal, etc.) was recorded as a new “referral” touch, overwriting the real source for the shopper’s next purchase. Add missing gateway domains under Settings → WooCommerce → Payment Gateway Domains.
  • Added: “Edit attribution” on the single-order screen to correct an order’s source/medium/campaign by hand (WC Analytics dashboards follow the edit), and a warning when the same gclid appears on several orders — a sign of one shared ad link.
  • Fixed: visits from Android apps (Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Telegram, etc.), Threads, and link-in-bio pages (Linktree, lnk.bio, Beacons) are now credited to that platform instead of ” / referral”.

1.27.2

  • Fixed: orders arriving with a product-feed UTM (utm_source=google_shopping, e.g. from Merchant Center feed links) were displayed as “google / cpc” — indistinguishable from Google Search. They now show as “google / shopping” when the visit carried a Google Ads click ID (a paid Shopping click), or “google_shopping / organic” when it did not (a free Shopping listing). Applies retroactively to existing orders and leads.
  • Changed: a Google Ads click ID (gclid) with no utm_medium is now recorded as “google / paid” instead of “google / cpc” — a click ID proves a paid Google click but not that it came from Search. Affects new visits only.
  • Changed: “shopping” now counts as a paid medium in Paid vs Organic reporting.

1.27.1

  • Fixed: the Leads dashboard’s summary cards (Attribution Rate, Top Source, Key Insights, Top Source/Medium/Campaign) always showed all-time totals, even when the table below was filtered to a specific date range. The summary now reflects the exact same date filter as the table.

1.27.0

  • Added: Source/Medium/Campaign filters on the WooCommerce Funnel, Campaign Performance, Cart Events, and Orders — Attribution screens are now select-from-list dropdowns (populated from your own tracked data) instead of free-text fields, so filtering no longer requires knowing the exact spelling of a value.
  • Docs: clarified in the Reporting API documentation that a SUMIT donation’s last_touch.medium can be a genuine empty string when a real source is known but no medium was ever provided — this is expected, not an error, for donation links that only include a source parameter.

1.26.1 and earlier

  • See docs/CHANGELOG-ARCHIVE.md for the complete history, including a Plugin Check SQL-interpolation annotation fix (1.26.1), the WooCommerce Analytics purchase/revenue consistency overhaul and Total Users metric (1.26.0), and everything before that.
